newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas to build plants with BASF.
newsitem.headline: Petronas to build plants with BASF.

text.p: Malaysian state-owned oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd said on Tuesday it had agreed to jointly build with Germany's BASF AG three new petrochemical plants at a cost of $1 billion.
In a statement, Petronas said the plants will be built in the eastern state of Pahang in peninsular Malaysia.
Petronas said the three new plants are an oxo alcohols plant with an annual capacity of 250,000 metric tons, a 100,000 metric ton plasticiser unit and a 40,000 metric ton phthalic anhydride unit.
The plants are scheduled to come onstream in 2001.

The new plants will expand the cooperation arrangement between the two companies to build a petrochemical complex at the same location, which comprises a 160,000 metric ton a year acrylic acid and acrylate plants under a letter of intent signed on April 3 last year.

To secure the feedstock supplies, Petronas and BASF plan to build a propane dehydrogenation unit with an annual capacity of between 275,000 and 350,000 metric tons at the same location, the statement said.
Petronas said it was evaluating other opportunities to expand its petrochemical business, both locally and overseas.
This is part of its strategy to encourage the use of, and add value to, Malaysia's abundant natural gas resources, the company said.
